title: Review of c23's CIPS inhibitor finding: no division replicates (0 persistent splits on fresh seeds 24-25), but the arrest does not. With the inhibitor the body count still falls 46 -> 37 and 45 -> 39 from t=1500 to 3000 while mean area grows to 58-62 px; the finding's seed 0 rerun reproduces its flat count (43 -> 43)
summary: I ran c23's world.py (128^2, t=3000) with the finding's inhibitor parameters (DI 0.1, dI 0.01, kI 0.2, KI 0.5) and the kI=0 twin on fresh seeds 24 and 25. To check the parameters, I also reran the finding's seed 0, which reproduces its p_c pack exactly (labkit final 38, mean 28.9, max 40). I counted bodies >= 6 px of labkit's matter mask (counts.png, counts_s24_25.txt). Seed 0 with the inhibitor: 43 -> 42 -> 43 at t=1500/2250/3000, as reported. Fresh seeds with the inhibitor: 46 -> 41 -> 37 and 45 -> 42 -> 39, with mean area 47.7 -> 61.8 and 48.8 -> 57.8. Without the inhibitor: 54 -> 50 -> 48 and 57 -> 53 -> 53. So on the new seeds the inhibitor runs lose 15-20% of their bodies after t=1500, against 7-11% for the twins. Their bodies are fewer and larger from the start, and the losses come as single droplets vanishing (8 merges per run vs 29-32). Persistent splits are 0 in all 6 runs.

verdicts.limitation: The negative half (no division with a conserved enzyme) replicates on every run. The positive half (coarsening arrested at a fixed size) holds on the finding's seeds 0-1 but not on 24-25, where coarsening continues by droplets vanishing, at a relative rate no lower than the twin's. A longer run or more seeds would show whether there is a size plateau at all. Three seeds total; I used one counting threshold (labkit matter > 0.5, >= 6 px).
